source.citation: Independent hand derivation from this repo's own 절기 calendar CSV and the classical 3-days-per-year rule (knowledge/08-luck-pillars.md), computed WITHOUT calling daeun.py: the calendar's 1946 row for 小暑 (next 節 after birth) is raw term_time 194607080206 — per E-1 (2026-09-25 audit), this is KST (UTC+9), so converted to the birth's own UTC-4 by subtracting 13h gives 1946-07-07 13:06 local. Elapsed from birth (1946-06-14 10:54 local) is 23 complete days; 23 // 3 = 7 (starting_age's own floor rule). 丙戌 year (Yang) + male → 순행 (forward); the month pillar 甲午 (idx 30 in the 60-cycle, cross-checked against the non-korean-longitude-trump PILLARS fixture in pillars.json, itself sourced from 사주매니아/fourpillars.net) steps forward by 1..8 in the JIAZI_CYCLE table (lookup.py) to give the period sequence below.
non-korean-longitude-trump (pillars.json) — same birth data, year/month/day pillars cross-checked against 사주매니아 and fourpillars.net (two independent calculators, both UTC-4 wartime Eastern War Time)

notes: F-12 (2026-09-26 audit): closes the validation gate's structural blind spot that EVERY daeun fixture used utc_offset 9.0 (KST), so a repeat of E-1's cross-timezone 절기-boundary bug in daeun.py's starting_age()/starting_age's term-boundary lookup would have been invisible to this gate. Reuses the already-externally-verified non-korean-longitude-trump birth (UTC-4, Queens NY) so the pillars are independently pinned elsewhere in this fixture set; the 대운 expectation itself is derived by hand (not sourced from a third-party 대운 table, since no cross-referenced non-Korean-birth 대운 publication was found), from the same calendar CSV + classical rule the engine itself is supposed to follow — so this fixture pins the ARITHMETIC, not merely the engine's current output.
